workload: Explain in three short sentences why duplicate sensor events can distort a rolling vibration average.
Explain in three short sentences why an industrial pump can have a high vibration reading without a confirmed failure.
Explain in three short sentences why a prediction score must identify the model and feature timestamp.

warmup.text: Duplicate sensor events can skew the rolling vibration average by inflating the total vibration value, leading to an overestimation of the actual vibration level. This distortion can result in inaccurate monitoring and potential misinterpretation of equipment health. Consequently, it's crucial to filter out duplicates to maintain the accuracy of the rolling average.

An industrial pump can exhibit high vibration readings due to misalignment between its shaft and motor. It may also be caused by loose or worn bearings, even if a definitive failure has not yet occurred. Additionally, vibration can increase with changes in fluid viscosity or flow rate without immediate mechanical damage being present.

A prediction score must identify the model used to ensure the score is interpretable and traceable to a specific algorithm. It must also specify the feature timestamp to account for the temporal dynamics of the data, ensuring the score reflects the most relevant conditions at the time of prediction. Lastly, this information is crucial for reproducibility
